warm_cache.methodology: Interleaved before/after runs with reversed order on alternate trials; fresh browser contexts, 1600x1000 viewport, external Google font CSS blocked equally. Startup ends at sb-ready plus two animation frames. Server transform caches are primed separately before timed trials. Fresh contexts have cold HTTP caches. first_distant_jump_ms includes fetching a previously unloaded last-slide chunk; sync_ms now awaits navigation and includes any on-demand requests. document_bytes is encoded HTML body bytes (gzip negotiated when supported); decoded_document_bytes is the full HTML size. Large cases include 20 scattered navigation calls, a real title edit followed by first and nine warm JSON state collections, five independent filmstrip scrolls, entering Scroll view and five distant main-deck jumps. Heap measurement follows a return to Focus. CPU_RATE optionally applies equal CDP CPU throttling to both versions. Timings exclude browser/server startup. engine_ms measures inline render/restore; initial useful layout is now deferred to the shell, so compare total startup and layout_ms as well. Durations are milliseconds; medians are across trials; no CPU profiler runs during timing.

cold_transform_cache.methodology: Five interleaved trials; fresh browser contexts and cold HTTP caches. Touch the exact fixture file before each request to invalidate the serving transform cache. Includes cache construction in startup; excludes launching browser/server processes. Same 1600x1000 viewport and font blocking as the warm-cache benchmark.

parallel_stress.methodology: Eight parallel fresh contexts; 10,000 slides, four viewport sizes, normal and 4x CPU throttling; 24 alternating focus/scroll jumps per context plus notes toggles. Functional assertions, not timing comparisons.

rust_assessment.reason: Warm UI time includes browser DOM/layout and JS bindings; no measured pure-compute kernel justifies a Rust rewrite. Cold split-cache construction is the concrete CPU candidate, incurred on a changed/evicted file; a persisted generated cache is a lower-complexity next experiment. No Rust speedup was benchmarked or claimed.
